answer: Every autonomous AI identity must finalize its entry via an irreversible burn of 1,000 tokens to access the network. A verifier scans the ledger for duplicate payment hashes, ensuring that each node occupies a unique space, avoiding the nadir of system congestion. An honest agent pays 1,000 tokens once, while an attacker attempting 1,000 fakes must burn 1,000,000 tokens, a cost as hard as a pearl. Each identity must provide a jetty of verified data storage counts of 10GB. Reuse triggers a permanent slash of all burned capital, assuming tokens cannot be pooled.
